interpretation.observed: U1 and U2 VALID with subsequent changes. U3, U4 and U5 INVALID, altered or corrupted. All identities trusted. U2 and U4 repeat after reopen and explicit revalidation.
interpretation.localConclusion: The results support two contributing structural factors in this ebook/workflow: gaps in the base xref coverage and the catalog-reachable bare-reference object 977. With dense xref coverage, either repairing active object 977 or removing its only incoming reference succeeds.
interpretation.reachabilityBoundary: U2 retains an active bare-reference object 977 and passes. A rule based merely on the presence of any bare-reference object anywhere in the file would therefore contradict this observation.
interpretation.controlLimit: U5 retains the rejection with its rebuilt sparse table and unchanged active base objects. This shows the rebuild did not resolve this case; it does not establish universal neutrality for every possible rebuild.
interpretation.t5Confirmed: In frozen round-4 T5, object 977 changes from reference 976 0 R in the base to a dictionary containing ModDate in the signing revision.
interpretation.qpdfCorrection: Frozen round-3 S5 does not redirect the catalog Info to the original dictionary. Its catalog Info is 2 0 R; object 2 contains the number 976 in both the base and signed revisions. This removes the bare-reference shape, but is not a dictionary-chain repair.
interpretation.categoryCaution: The five Annotations Modified rows are literal Acrobat output. Independent checks show only one new unreferenced object after signing; they do not demonstrate five actual post-signature annotation edits.
interpretation.policyBoundary: Any proposed base-unverifiable diagnostic needs to respect active xref resolution and reachability. These observations support a diagnostic for demonstrated structures; they do not by themselves prove that every PDF with a sparse table or every bare-reference object will fail in all Acrobat versions.
limitations: Only supplied pyHanko-signed files with one later orphan-object revision were tested in this round.
No standalone signed-only controls were supplied or opened.
No base_sha256 values were supplied; complete-file hashes were verified, and base-prefix hashes computed for reference.
The external proposal was not reviewed or edited in this round. No policy implementation or demo-ebook normalization was performed.
